source.title: EVALUATION OF COMPLEXITY MEASURES FOR DEEP LEARNING GENERALIZATION IN MEDICAL IMAGE ANALYSIS

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendix, is present. No apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extracting the relevant findings.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures PAC-Bayes flatness and its correlation with generalization gaps, extending that measure to medical-image classifiers and datasets.
record.gate_note: The paper tests complexity measures against generalization performance. Its depth sweeps and single-task/multi-task comparisons are not tests of the listed width, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, or dropout versions. It does not test memorization of random labels.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates magnitude-aware sharpness against generalization gaps in a new setting: VGG-like classifiers on breast ultrasound images. Experiment 1 compares models trained to the same 1% training error; Experiments 2 and 3 extend the analysis to early-stopped models with unequal training errors.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they favor magnitude-aware PAC-Bayes flatness, identify useful spectral- and path-based measures, and report improved generalization with multi-task learning. However, their consistency claim combines gap correlations in Experiment 1 with test-risk correlations in Experiments 2 and 3; magnitude-aware flatness does not correlate positively with the gap across all three experiments.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates the PAC-Bayes flatness measure on VGG-like medical-image classifiers. It uses breast ultrasound datasets, depth variation, and Kendall correlations rather than the claim's stated CIFAR-10 and SVHN setting.
record.method_sensitivity: The magnitude-aware flatness correlation with excess risk changes across experiment settings: it is positive in the fully converged, unregularized single-task experiment and negative in the early-stopped single-task and multi-task experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Magnitude-aware sharpness correlates positively with test risk in Experiments 2 and 3 (0.381 and 0.211), despite negative correlations with generalization gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Magnitude-aware sharpness can track held-out error in early-stopped medical-image classifiers even when it does not track the training–test gap.

fits_no_version.finding: The study reports improved classification performance from joint classification and segmentation on held-out BUSIS images and external datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Joint segmentation and classification can improve breast-ultrasound classification generalization relative to classification alone.

record.peer_reviewed: International Workshop on Machine Learning for Signal Processing
record.problems: The experiments use breast ultrasound datasets and VGG-like models. Experiments 2 and 3 use early stopping and additional regularization, unlike Experiment 1, and the paper attributes the Experiment 2 gap pattern partly to underfitting. The correlation coefficients have no uncertainty estimates stated in the table.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for V7 were left out. The study reports correlations for many other complexity measures, but those do not directly report the magnitude-aware flatness measure named in V7.

untested.parts: No random-label training or natural-label versus random-label comparison.
No controlled width sweep beyond the width needed to interpolate; the study varies depth and associated architecture sizes.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
No optimizer comparison; all experiments use Adam.
No isolated dropout comparison; dropout accompanies other changes in regularization and experimental design.
The original CIFAR-10/SVHN setting is not replicated. Experiments 2 and 3 do not test the relationship among models trained to similarly low training loss.
No identification or removal of memorized examples.

missing.what: Experiment 1's granulated Kendall coefficient for magnitude-aware flatness is 0.533, supporting the relationship across architecture groups.

Record the comparison underlying V7's ranking component: magnitude-aware flatness has Kendall correlation 0.491, versus at most 0.462 among tested spectral-norm measures, 0.234 and 0.281 for path measures, and 0.290 for inverse margin.
The robust analysis explicitly identifies magnitude-aware PAC-Bayes flatness as achieving the best overall correlation. Exact bar values are unavailable in the supplied figure text.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V7. Correlations have no reported uncertainty estimates. The appendix defines the measure as inverse magnitude-scaled perturbation variance with expected perturbed training error at most 0.1; its prose describing a reduction in risk is inconsistent with that equation.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not train on random labels or compare natural-label and random-label generalization.
It varies network depth, not width beyond the interpolation threshold.
It does not compare convolutional and fully connected architectures.
It uses Adam throughout and does not compare optimizers.
It uses a mini-batch of 2 in Experiment 1 and does not compare batch sizes.
Dropout is present only alongside other regularization in Experiment 2; its effect is not isolated.
The study uses VGG-like classifiers on breast ultrasound datasets, not the stated CIFAR-10 and SVHN setting. It does not establish causation.
It does not identify or remove memorized training examples.

relationships.condition: Experiment 1: unregularized single-task BUS-Combined classifiers trained to 1% training error
relationships.reason: R1 reports a positive gap correlation of 0.491; Table 1 also shows this exceeds every tested norm- and margin-based measure in this setting.
relationships.display_finding: Magnitude-aware sharpness correlated positively with the generalization gap (τ = 0.491). The available evidence does not confirm its reported advantage over norm and margin measures.
